page_title: Interview with Betsy Beyer, Stephen Thorne of Google

sources.entry: Interview with Betsy Beyer, Stephen Thorne of Google

summary.name: Interview with Betsy Beyer and Stephen Thorne (SRE)
summary.one_liner: An interview with two Google SRE book authors covering how Site Reliability Engineering relates to DevOps, error budgets, blameless postmortems, toil, and SRE antipatterns.
use_cases: Deciding how to set an error budget policy with management
Learning how SRE fits within a DevOps practice
Capping operational toil on an engineering team
Planning disaster recovery or incident-response training exercises
Avoiding common SRE anti-patterns in an organization
summary.what_it_does: The page is a written interview with Google SRE Betsy Beyer and Stephen Thorne, excerpted for an upcoming Apress book on DevOps. It explains that SRE is a specific implementation of DevOps principles and describes using error budgets to decide when to speed up or slow down releases. It covers blameless postmortems, including when to run them and how to prioritize action items. It also describes practices such as the Wheel of Misfortune exercise, DIRT disaster testing, and a cap of 50% of SRE time on toil. The page lists several SRE books and a free online SRE book as references.
notable: Describes error budget policies as a written, pre-agreed rule that management enforces
Explains the Wheel of Misfortune tabletop incident-response exercise
Recommends capping toil at about 50% of SRE time
caveats: Written as an interview excerpt, not a tool; it describes practices and does not offer software
Describes Google's internal practices, which the authors note may not apply directly to other companies
Refers to a forthcoming book whose details are not confirmed on the page
